description:
IA-QA as an MCP Server
Use IA-QA's developer tools to test your llm agents RAG ai tools, directly from Cursor, Claude Desktop, Windsurf, or any AI agent without leaving your IDE. 
Many classical testing tools too ! Enjoy ! 
No API key. No signup. Free.

tool_signatures.name: ab_test_report
tool_signatures.description: Generate an A/B test report comparing two prompts or model configurations. Accepts arrays of scores and returns statistical comparison: mean, median, std deviation, winner, and improvement percentage.

variant_a.description: First variant configuration with name and score array

variant_b.description: Second variant configuration with name and score array

tool_signatures.name: analyze_diff_bugs
tool_signatures.description: Pattern-based diff linter: flags a fixed set of risky shapes in changed code — query-string interpolation (SQL/Cypher/Mongo injection shape), shell interpolation, eval/new Function, empty catch blocks, regex built from a variable, fewer catch blocks than before, and named authorization guards that disappeared. Every finding cites the line that produced it. It does NOT do data-flow analysis: it cannot follow a value to a sink, across functions or files, and an empty result is not a safety verdict (the response lists what it did not analyse). Advisory triage — use a static analyser for a real security gate.

context.description: Optional PR title or feature context for better analysis

version1.description: Original code (before changes). If omitted, only the new version is analysed.

tool_signatures.name: analyze_responses
tool_signatures.description: Semantically analyze N already-produced model outputs for the SAME task (the MCP counterpart to the LLM Sandbox). Without a reference: computes consensus — pairwise cosine agreement, the most-representative output, and the outlier. With a `reference` (ground truth): also ranks every output by closeness (token cosine + ROUGE-L composite) and names the closest. Deterministic, no LLM, no key — gate-able in CI. You bring the outputs (2+). For a 2-way head-to-head with structural JSON diff use compare_responses instead.

reference.description: Optional ground-truth answer. If set, each output is also ranked by closeness to it and the closest one is named.

label.description: Human name for this candidate (e.g. model id)

responses.description: The outputs to analyze (same task, N models/prompts/versions). Each item is a plain string or { "label": "GPT-4o", "text": "..." }. At least 2 required.

tool_signatures.name: base64_decode
tool_signatures.description: Decode a Base64 string back to UTF-8 text. Use for inspecting Base64-encoded API responses, JWT payload claims, config file values, or attachment data.

tool_signatures.name: base64_encode
tool_signatures.description: Encode a UTF-8 string to Base64. Use when you need to embed binary data, multi-line text, or special characters safely inside JSON fields, HTTP headers, or data URIs.

tool_signatures.name: bias_detect
tool_signatures.description: Analyse a set of LLM responses generated from the same prompt template but with different demographic variants (gender, origin, age, tone). Returns a bias score (0-100), sentiment analysis per variant, pairwise Jaccard similarity, and a human-readable verdict. No API key needed — runs entirely locally.

answer.description: The LLM response text for this variant

responses.description: Array of variant responses to compare for bias

tool_signatures.name: bm25_score
tool_signatures.description: Compute BM25 relevance score between a query and one or more documents. BM25 is the industry-standard keyword-based ranking algorithm used in Elasticsearch, OpenSearch, and Weaviate hybrid search. Returns ranked results with normalized scores.

tool_signatures.name: build_rag_prompt
tool_signatures.description: Assemble a complete RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) prompt from retrieved context chunks and a user query. Handles token budgeting, citation numbering, system instruction injection, and source attribution.

system_instruction.description: Custom system instruction (default: standard RAG grounding instruction)

tool_signatures.name: calculate_readability
tool_signatures.description: Calculate readability scores: Flesch Reading Ease, Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level, Coleman-Liau Index, and Automated Readability Index. Useful for evaluating LLM output quality.

tool_signatures.name: case_convert
tool_signatures.description: Convert a string between naming conventions: camelCase, PascalCase, snake_case, kebab-case, UPPER_SNAKE_CASE, dot.case, Title Case. Essential for code generation and refactoring.

tool_signatures.name: check_contrast_ratio
tool_signatures.description: Calculate WCAG 2.1 contrast ratio between two colors. Returns ratio and compliance for AA/AAA normal and large text.

tool_signatures.name: color_convert
tool_signatures.description: Convert a color between HEX, RGB, and HSL formats. Use when translating design tokens between CSS notations, verifying color accessibility, or normalizing color values from user input. Accepts #rrggbb, #rgb, rgb(r,g,b), or hsl(h,s%,l%).

tool_signatures.name: compare_models
tool_signatures.description: Compare 2-5 AI models side by side: context window, pricing, multimodal, reasoning capabilities, and provider. Returns a comparison table with a recommendation based on your use case.

tool_signatures.name: compare_responses
tool_signatures.description: Compare two ALREADY-PRODUCED outputs (e.g. model A vs model B on the same task) side by side. Returns deterministic metrics (token cosine, ROUGE-L, Jaccard, length/structure deltas, JSON diff) and a verdict. If a `reference` (ground truth) is given, scores each output against it and picks the closer one. If `model` + `api_key` are given, an LLM judge also picks a qualitative winner for the task. No re-execution — you bring the outputs.

task.description: The task/prompt both outputs were answering — used by the LLM judge for context

model.description: Optional judge model id (BYOK). When set with api_key, an LLM judge picks a qualitative winner.

api_key.description: Optional API key for the judge model (BYOK). Used only for the judge call; never stored.

reference.description: Optional ground-truth / expected answer. If set, each output is scored against it and the closer one wins (deterministic).

check_json.description: Try to parse as JSON and compare structurally (keys, types, values)

tool_signatures.name: consistency_check
tool_signatures.description: Compare multiple LLM responses to the same prompt and detect inconsistencies using Jaccard word-overlap similarity and fact drift (number comparison). Fast, deterministic, no API key needed. Limitations: relies on surface-level word matching — "Paris is the capital of France" vs "Paris is the French capital" may score low despite semantic equivalence. For true semantic consistency, use run_semantic_tests with embedding mode. Essential for determinism testing.

responses.description: Array of 2+ LLM responses to compare (same prompt, different runs)

check_facts.description: Check for contradictory numbers/facts across responses (default: true)

tool_signatures.name: context_window_check
tool_signatures.description: Given an array of message objects [{role, content}], estimate total token usage and check if it fits in the target model's context window. Warns about truncation risk.

tool_signatures.name: conversation_analyze
tool_signatures.description: Analyze a multi-turn conversation for context retention, topic drift, instruction following, and repetition. Accepts messages array [{role, content}]. Essential for chatbot QA.

tool_signatures.name: cookie_security_audit
tool_signatures.description: Audit the security attributes of cookies set by any URL. Fetches the URL and inspects all Set-Cookie headers for: HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite, Domain scope, Path scope, Max-Age/Expires, __Host-/__Secure- prefixes. Flags insecure patterns: missing HttpOnly on session cookies, missing Secure flag, SameSite=None without Secure, overly broad Domain, and excessive TTL. Returns per-cookie grades and an overall security score (0–100).

tool_signatures.name: cors_checker
tool_signatures.description: Check the CORS configuration of a URL the same way a browser would. Returns the main response status, all Access-Control-* headers, the tested origin, and the preflight OPTIONS response. Use this for direct CORS debugging, not just security auditing.

url.description: Full URL to test, e.g. https://api.example.com/resource

tool_signatures.name: cors_test
tool_signatures.description: Test a URL for CORS misconfigurations. Sends preflight (OPTIONS) and cross-origin requests with various Origin headers to detect: wildcard origins with credentials, origin reflection (echoing any origin), null origin acceptance, subdomain wildcard bypass, and missing Vary headers. Returns risk level (safe/low/medium/high/critical), per-test results, and fix recommendations. Essential for API security audits.

origin.description: Custom Origin header to test (default: tests multiple origins automatically)

tool_signatures.name: cot_analyzer
tool_signatures.description: Analyze a Chain-of-Thought (CoT) or reasoning trace from an LLM. Detects step count, logical flow, conclusion presence, backtracking, and estimates reasoning depth. Useful for o1/o3/DeepSeek-R1 evaluation.

reasoning.description: The CoT / reasoning trace text (e.g. from <think> tags or step-by-step output)

expected_conclusion.description: Expected final answer to check against (optional)

tool_signatures.name: count_code_lines
tool_signatures.description: Count lines of code: total, code lines, comment lines, blank lines, and comment density. Supports JS/TS, Python, Java/C/C++, Ruby, Go, Shell, HTML/XML, and CSS.

tool_signatures.name: count_tokens
tool_signatures.description: Estimate the token count of a text string using the cl100k_base approximation (~4 chars/token). Call this BEFORE sending any text to an LLM API to check if it fits within the model context window and to estimate cost. Returns token estimate, character count, and word count.

tool_signatures.name: create_confluence_page
tool_signatures.description: Create a new Confluence page from the output of jira_to_test_suite. Formats Gherkin, E2E steps, API tests, and test data as a properly structured Confluence page with code blocks and tables. STATEFUL — creates a new page in the specified space.

issue_key.description: Source Jira issue key (for the page title and source link)

issue_url.description: Source Jira issue URL (added as a link in the page)

space_key.description: Confluence space key where the page will be created, e.g. "QA", "ENG"

test_suite.description: The test_suite object from jira_to_test_suite result

parent_page_id.description: Optional parent page ID — page will be created as a child of this page

tool_signatures.name: cron_parse
tool_signatures.description: Parse a cron expression into a human-readable schedule description. Supports standard 5-field cron (minute hour day month weekday).

tool_signatures.name: cron_validator
tool_signatures.description: Validate a 5-field cron expression, explain the schedule, and preview the next execution times. Use this to debug cron jobs before they reach production. Returns parsed fields, a human-readable description, and upcoming ISO timestamps.

next_runs_count.description: How many upcoming runs to return (1-50, default: 10)

tool_signatures.name: decode_jwt
tool_signatures.description: Decode a JWT (JSON Web Token) and return its header and payload without verifying the signature. Also reports whether the token is expired and the exact expiry date. Use to inspect claims (sub, iss, exp, roles) during debugging or when integrating with an auth provider.

tool_signatures.name: detect_language
tool_signatures.description: Detect the natural language of a text using n-gram frequency analysis and common word markers. Supports 15 languages: English, French, Spanish, German, Italian, Portuguese, Dutch, Russian, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Arabic, Polish, Turkish, Swedish.

input.description: Text to detect language from (min 20 chars for accuracy)

tool_signatures.name: detect_secrets
tool_signatures.description: Scan code or config files for hardcoded secrets: AWS keys, GitHub tokens, OpenAI/Anthropic API keys, Stripe secrets, JWTs, database connection strings, and generic passwords. Returns findings with severity. Run before every commit.

input.description: Code or config content to scan (max 500KB)

tool_signatures.name: diff_mappings
tool_signatures.description: Diff a baseline page mapping against a current one and return a CI-style verdict: PASS / FIX / BLOCK, plus per-element drift (ok, renamed, healable, ambiguous, lost, added, rebound). Pure and deterministic — provide two mappings as JSON with "elements" arrays of {role, name, selector, context?}. Use the companion @ia-qa/self-healing package (npm install -g @ia-qa/self-healing) to capture mappings from your app via its local MCP server ia-qa-heal-mcp, or paste the snippet from ia-qa.com/devtools/selector-drift into your browser console.

after.description: Current page mapping: same shape as before, captured after the UI change.

before.description: Baseline page mapping: { page, url, capturedAt, elements: [{role, name, selector, context?}] }. Captured before a UI change.

tool_signatures.name: diff_text
tool_signatures.description: Compute a unified line-by-line diff between two text strings (LCS algorithm). Returns added/removed/unchanged line counts and formatted diff hunks with configurable context lines (0–20). Use to compare versions of prompts, configs, code snippets, or any text where you need to see exactly what changed.

context.description: Context lines around each change (0–20, default: 3)

tool_signatures.name: embedding_similarity
tool_signatures.description: Compute text similarity using local algorithms (Bag of Words, TF-IDF, Character N-grams). No API key needed — runs entirely in-process. NOT real embeddings: for true semantic similarity with vector embeddings, use run_semantic_tests with mode="embeddings" and your OpenAI API key. Supports single pair or batch mode with pipe-separated pairs. Useful for RAG retrieval testing, semantic search evaluation, and text deduplication.

batch.description: Batch mode: array of { text_a, text_b } pairs. Overrides text_a/text_b if provided.

methods.description: Algorithms to use (default: all three). Options: "bow", "tfidf", "ngram"

tool_signatures.name: env_parse
tool_signatures.description: Parse a .env file content into a JSON object. Handles quoted values (single and double), inline comments, export prefix, and escaped sequences (\n, \t inside double quotes). Returns all key-value pairs. Use in CI/CD pipelines, agent config loaders, or when processing dotenv files programmatically.

input.description: .env file content to parse (e.g. the output of `cat .env`)

tool_signatures.name: escape_html
tool_signatures.description: Escape HTML special characters (&, <, >, ", ') to their safe HTML entities. ALWAYS call this before inserting any user-provided or LLM-generated content into an HTML template to prevent cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks.

tool_signatures.name: estimate_llm_cost
tool_signatures.description: Estimate the API cost in USD for a given model and token counts. Supports all major 2024–2026 models: GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, o3, o4-mini, Claude Opus 4, Claude Sonnet 4/4.5, Gemini 2.5 Pro/Flash, DeepSeek V3/R1, Grok 3, and legacy models.

tool_signatures.name: extract_json_from_text
tool_signatures.description: Extract the first valid JSON object or array embedded in chaotic LLM output (surrounded by markdown fences, prose, or explanatory text). Handles ```json blocks and inline JSON. Call this whenever an LLM returns structured data mixed with explanation text instead of raw JSON.

input.description: Raw text (e.g., LLM output) that may contain a JSON object or array

tool_signatures.name: extract_json_path
tool_signatures.description: Extract a value from a JSON string using dot-notation path (e.g., "user.address.city", "items.0.name", "meta.tags"). Supports array index access via numeric path segments.

input.description: The JSON to traverse — a JSON string, or the object/array itself.

tool_signatures.name: extract_links
tool_signatures.description: Extract all URLs, email addresses, and domain names from text. Returns categorized and deduplicated results. Useful for content auditing, link checking, and web scraping validation.

tool_signatures.name: extract_todos
tool_signatures.description: Extract TODO, FIXME, HACK, BUG, NOTE, OPTIMIZE, and custom tags from any source code or text. Returns line numbers, tag types, and message text. Essential for technical debt auditing.

tags.description: Custom tags to add (default set: TODO, FIXME, HACK, NOTE, BUG, OPTIMIZE, XXX)

tool_signatures.name: fetch_confluence_page
tool_signatures.description: Fetch a Confluence page and return its content as clean Markdown. Accepts a numeric page_id or a full page URL. Optionally lists direct child pages. BYOK — credentials transit in-memory only, never stored.

page_url.description: Full Confluence page URL (alternative to page_id), e.g. "https://mycompany.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/123456789"

confluence_email.description: Atlassian account email (same credentials as Jira)

include_children.description: List direct child pages (id + title) (default: false)

tool_signatures.name: fetch_jira_issue
tool_signatures.description: Fetch a complete Jira issue: summary, description converted to Markdown, status, assignee, priority, labels, custom fields, and optionally comments and attachment metadata. BYOK — credentials transit in-memory only, never stored on ia-qa.com.

fields.description: Specific Jira field names to return. Omit for all standard fields.

jira_token.description: Atlassian API token (from id.atlassian.com > Security > API tokens)

include_comments.description: Include issue comments, up to 20 (default: true)

tool_signatures.name: fetch_veille_feed
tool_signatures.description: Fetch the latest QA & AI/LLM articles aggregated from curated RSS sources (Google Testing Blog, DEV.to Testing/QA/AI/LLM/Agents, Hugging Face Blog, Simon Willison). Perfect for agents monitoring the QA & AI landscape.

tool_signatures.name: few_shot_formatter
tool_signatures.description: Format few-shot examples for LLM prompts. Converts example pairs into formatted blocks. Supports chat format (User/Assistant), XML tags, Markdown, or plain text.

tool_signatures.name: find_tool
tool_signatures.description: Search available MCP tools by keyword or category before calling them. Returns matching tool names, descriptions, and optionally their inputSchemas. Call this when you are unsure which tool to use or want to explore the catalogue. Categories: data, encoding, text, llm, qa, rag, dev, security, web.

query.description: Keyword(s) to search in tool name and description (e.g. "cors", "token", "vector", "json")

category.description: Optional: filter by category — data | encoding | text | llm | qa | rag | dev | security | web

max_results.description: Maximum tools to return (default 10, max 50). Results are ranked by IDF-weighted relevance, so common words like "test" do not inflate the list.

with_schema.description: Set true to include inputSchema in results (default: false)

tool_signatures.name: fix_gherkin
tool_signatures.description: Fix Gherkin syntax warnings from a jira_to_test_suite result. Takes the current gherkin text and the _gherkin_warnings array, calls your LLM to fix ONLY the flagged issues (adds missing Given/When/Then steps, etc.), and returns the corrected Gherkin. Lightweight — uses ~300-500 tokens vs ~5k for a full regeneration. Requires BYOK LLM key.

model.description: LLM model to use for the fix, e.g. "gpt-4o-mini". Must belong to the provider whose key you passed in api_key.

api_key.description: Your own LLM provider API key (BYOK) — OpenAI "sk-…", Anthropic "sk-ant-…", Google "AIzaSy…", or Groq "gsk_…". There is no server-side key for this tool: if you do not have one, do not call it and do not invent a value — placeholders like "configured", "your_api_key" or a masked "sk-…***…" are rejected. Used for this call only, never stored.

gherkin.description: The current Gherkin text from the jira_to_test_suite result (test_suite.gherkin).

warnings.description: The _gherkin_warnings array from the jira_to_test_suite result.

tool_signatures.name: flatten_json
tool_signatures.description: Flatten a nested JSON object to single-level dot-notation keys (e.g. {"a":{"b":1}} → {"a.b":1}), or unflatten dot-notation keys back to a nested object. Supports custom separators.

input.description: The JSON to flatten or unflatten — a JSON string, or the object itself.

tool_signatures.name: format_bytes
tool_signatures.description: Convert raw byte counts to human-readable sizes in SI (KB=1000) or IEC (KiB=1024) units, or parse size strings back to bytes. Covers B, KB/KiB, MB/MiB, GB/GiB, TB/TiB, PB/PiB.

size_string.description: Size string to parse to bytes (e.g. "1.5 GB", "512 MiB")

tool_signatures.name: format_json
tool_signatures.description: Validate and pretty-print a string that is ALREADY valid JSON. Strict by design — it is a validity gate: valid JSON comes back formatted, anything else is rejected with the exact parse error. It never repairs, completes, or guesses. NOT for: plain text or prose (will fail), JSON embedded in markdown/prose (use extract_json_from_text first), JS objects (JSON.stringify them first), YAML (use yaml_to_json).

input.description: A raw JSON string, e.g. '{"key":"value"}'. Must already parse as JSON — plain text or truncated JSON is rejected, not repaired.

tool_signatures.name: format_table
tool_signatures.description: Convert a JSON array of objects into a Markdown table. Automatically detects columns, aligns headers, and fills missing keys with empty cells. Use when an agent needs to present structured data — tool results, model comparisons, test reports — as a readable table in a response or document.

input.description: The array of objects to render — a JSON string, or the array itself.

columns.description: Column names and order (default: all keys from first row)

tool_signatures.name: function_call_validate
tool_signatures.description: Validate an LLM function call / tool_use output: check that function name is in allowed list, arguments match expected schema, no extra/missing args. For OpenAI function calling & MCP tool_use testing.

function_call.description: The function call object from LLM (e.g. { "name": "get_weather", "arguments": {"city":"Paris"} })

tool_signatures.name: generate_ci_workflow
tool_signatures.description: Generate a ready-to-commit GitHub Actions workflow that gates a build on IA-QA. Two gate types, combinable: "eval_contract" runs a .ia-eval.yaml through ia-qa-com/eval-action@v1 (LLM quality gate, needs a provider API key as a repo secret), and "cli_checks" runs deterministic primitives via npx @ia-qa/cli (secret scan, prompt-injection scan, security headers…) whose exit code fails the build. Deterministic template — no LLM call, no API key, same inputs give the same file. Returns the YAML, the secrets to create, and the remaining steps. Pair with generate_eval_yaml to produce the contract itself.

cron.description: Cron expression when triggers include 'schedule' (default: '0 6 * * 1' — Mondays 06:00 UTC).

gate.description: Which gate to emit. eval_contract = LLM eval via the action (default). cli_checks = deterministic CLI assertions. both = CLI checks first, eval last.

provider.description: LLM provider the contract runs against — decides which repository secret the workflow wires (default: groq).

cli_tools.description: IA-QA tool names to run as deterministic gates, e.g. ["secret_scan","prompt_injection_scan"]. Tools with no known CI recipe get a --stdin step flagged in notes.

min_score.description: Override the contract min_score (0-100). Omit to use the value in the contract.

fail_on_fail.description: Fail the build on a FAIL/PARTIAL verdict (default: true). Set false to report without gating.

node_version.description: Node version for the CLI steps (default: "20").

contract_path.description: Path to the .ia-eval.yaml contract, relative to the repo root (default: evals/smoke.ia-eval.yaml). Only used when the gate includes eval_contract.

tool_signatures.name: generate_curl
tool_signatures.description: Generate a curl command from request parameters. Supports GET/POST/PUT/DELETE, custom headers, JSON body, and form data. Useful for documentation, sharing, and debugging API calls.

tool_signatures.name: generate_eval_yaml
tool_signatures.description: Generate a complete .ia-eval.yaml evaluation contract from a plain-language description of what your LLM should do. Uses Groq llama-3.3-70b (server-side, no API key needed). Returns ready-to-run YAML for the LLM Test Runner (run_eval_contract). Picks appropriate evaluators (cosine_similarity, contains_check, hallucination_check, etc.) based on the task type.

task_type.description: Optional task type hint to guide evaluator selection.

description.description: Plain-language description of what the LLM under test should do. Be specific: describe inputs, expected behaviour, and constraints.

system_prompt.description: Optional system prompt of the LLM under test. Helps generate more accurate test cases.

scenario_count.description: Number of scenarios to generate (default: 5). Covers happy path + edge cases + adversarial.

tool_signatures.name: generate_hmac
tool_signatures.description: Compute an HMAC signature for a message using a secret key. Supports SHA-256 (default), SHA-512, SHA-1, and MD5. Used for API request signing, webhook verification (GitHub, Stripe, Twilio), and JWT validation.

algorithm.description: Hash algorithm: sha256 (default), sha512, sha1, md5

tool_signatures.name: generate_html_report
tool_signatures.description: Convert a run_eval_contract() LLM Test Runner JSON result into a fully self-contained dark-themed HTML report with Pass/Fail badges, side-by-side Input/Output/Ground-Truth panels, evaluator score bars, and a radar chart. Returns the HTML as a string.

results.description: The JSON object returned by run_eval_contract()

tool_signatures.name: generate_json_ld
tool_signatures.description: Generate a ready-to-paste <script type="application/ld+json"> snippet for GEO / structured data optimization. Supported types: WebSite, FAQPage, Article, Person, Organization, SoftwareApplication, HowTo.

fields.description: Schema fields as key-value pairs (name, url, description, author, datePublished, etc.)

faq_items.description: For FAQPage/HowTo: array of { question, answer } objects

tool_signatures.name: generate_password
tool_signatures.description: Generate a cryptographically secure random password using crypto.randomBytes. Configurable length (4–128), uppercase letters, digits, and symbols. Use when resetting user passwords, seeding test accounts, or generating API secrets.

tool_signatures.name: generate_slug
tool_signatures.description: Convert any string into a URL-friendly slug: lowercase, ASCII-normalized (é→e), special characters removed, spaces replaced with hyphens. Use for generating SEO-friendly URL paths, file names, or identifier keys from user-provided titles or labels.

tool_signatures.name: generate_test_cases
tool_signatures.description: Generate a set of test cases (valid, edge, invalid) for a given feature description. Returns test matrix with Gherkin scenarios ready to use.

inputs.description: Optional: list of input parameters (one per line, e.g. "email: string [required]")

feature.description: Feature or function to test. Be specific: describe inputs, expected behaviour, context.

tool_signatures.name: generate_uuid
tool_signatures.description: Generate one or more cryptographically random UUID v4 identifiers. Use this when you need unique IDs for test fixtures, database records, session tokens, or any scenario requiring a guaranteed-unique string. Returns up to 100 UUIDs in one call.

count.description: Number of UUIDs to generate (1–100, default: 1)

tool_signatures.name: get_testing_guidelines
tool_signatures.description: Query the IA-QA methodology knowledge base. Returns structured testing guidelines, assertion strategies, thresholds, best practices, and relevant MCP tools for a given topic. Call without a topic to list all available topics. Topics: llm-unit-testing, rag-pipeline, prompt-stability, prompt-ab-testing, embedding-quality, eval-framework, semantic-testing, auto-testing, security, api-testing, ci-cd, multimodal, llm-data-security, agent-observability, pro-tips, learning-paths, golden-dataset.

topic.description: The testing topic to retrieve guidelines for. Omit to get the full list of available topics.

tool_signatures.name: guardrail_test
tool_signatures.description: Test an LLM response against a set of guardrail rules: must-include, must-not-include, max length, required format, language, forbidden patterns, and custom regex. Returns pass/fail per rule.

value.description: Value for the rule (text, number as string, regex, or format name)

rules.description: Array of guardrail rules to check

tool_signatures.name: hallucination_check
tool_signatures.description: Word-overlap based hallucination check: verifies if an LLM answer's words and numbers appear in the provided source/context. Fast, deterministic, no API key needed. Limitations: not semantic — does not understand synonyms or paraphrases. For true semantic grounding, use run_semantic_tests with embedding mode. Essential for quick RAG accuracy testing.

strict.description: If true, every sentence in the answer must be supported (default: false)

context.description: The source/reference text that should ground the answer

tool_signatures.name: hash_text
tool_signatures.description: Compute a cryptographic hash of a text string. Use when you need to verify data integrity, generate content fingerprints, hash passwords (prefer SHA-256+), or produce a fixed-length digest of any input. Supports SHA-256 (default), SHA-512, SHA-1, and MD5.

algorithm.description: Hash algorithm: sha256 (default), sha512, sha1, md5

tool_signatures.name: html_to_markdown
tool_signatures.description: Convert HTML to clean Markdown. Strips scripts, styles, nav, ads, and comments. Converts headings, lists, links, images, code blocks. Ideal for preparing web content as LLM context.

strip_links.description: Strip link URLs, keep text only (default: false)

tool_signatures.name: http_status_lookup
tool_signatures.description: Look up detailed information about any HTTP status code: class, name, description, cacheability, typical causes, and handling best practices. Covers all standard 1xx-5xx codes.

tool_signatures.name: identify_caller
tool_signatures.description: Returns what the server knows about the current MCP client: clientInfo captured during initialize, User-Agent, and any _meta fields sent with this request. Useful for debugging caller identification.

_meta.description: Optional self-identification. Keys: agent (string), model (string), version (string).

tool_signatures.name: jira_to_test_suite
tool_signatures.description: Transform a Jira ticket into a complete test suite: Gherkin scenarios, E2E steps, API test cases, test data matrix, and ambiguity detection. Accepts either Jira credentials (auto-fetch) or a pre-fetched issue object. The returned test_suite includes _gherkin_warnings (deterministic syntax validation — empty if clean). Requires BYOK LLM key (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.).

issue.description: Pre-fetched issue object from fetch_jira_issue, OR a mock object with fields: key, summary, description (plain text or Markdown), status, issue_type, priority, labels, comments. Use this for offline/CI testing without Jira credentials.

api_key.description: Your LLM provider API key (OpenAI sk-, Anthropic sk-ant-, Google AIzaSy-, etc.).

issue_key.description: Jira issue key to fetch automatically, e.g. "PROJ-123". Required if issue is not provided.

jira_email.description: Atlassian account email. Required for auto-fetch mode.

jira_token.description: Atlassian API token. Required for auto-fetch mode.

max_tokens.description: Maximum tokens for the LLM response. Default: 8192. Increase for large tickets with many ACs; decrease to reduce cost on simple tickets.

jira_base_url.description: Atlassian base URL. Required for auto-fetch mode.

confluence_pages.description: Optional array of pre-fetched Confluence page objects from fetch_confluence_page, used as documentation context.

tool_signatures.name: json_diff
tool_signatures.description: Compute a deep structural diff between two JSON values. Returns added, removed, and changed keys with dot-notation paths. Like git diff but for JSON objects — perfect for API response regression testing.

after.description: The modified JSON (after) — a JSON string, or the value itself.

before.description: The original JSON (before) — a JSON string, or the value itself.

tool_signatures.name: json_schema_generate
tool_signatures.description: Infer a JSON Schema (draft-07) from a sample JSON value. Detects types, required fields, array item shapes, nested objects, and common string formats (email, uri, date, date-time, uuid). Returns a ready-to-use schema compatible with json_schema_validate. Use when you have a sample API response or LLM output and want to auto-generate a validation schema for CI/CD testing.

input.description: The sample JSON value to infer the schema from — a JSON string, or the value itself.

required_all.description: Mark all detected object properties as required (default: true)

tool_signatures.name: json_schema_validate
tool_signatures.description: Validate a JSON value against a JSON Schema (draft-07 subset). Supports type, required, properties, items, enum, const, pattern, format (email/uri/date), minimum/maximum, minLength/maxLength, minItems/maxItems, uniqueItems, additionalProperties, anyOf, allOf, oneOf. Returns all validation errors with dot-notation paths.

value.description: The JSON value to validate — a JSON string, or the value itself.

schema.description: The JSON Schema — a JSON string, or the schema object itself.

tool_signatures.name: json_to_csv
tool_signatures.description: Convert a JSON array of objects to CSV format. Automatically detects columns from all object keys. Handles quoting and escaping per RFC 4180.

input.description: The array of objects to convert — a JSON string, or the array itself.

tool_signatures.name: json_to_yaml
tool_signatures.description: Convert a JSON object to clean, human-readable YAML. Handles nested objects, arrays, multiline strings, and special characters. No external dependencies.

input.description: The JSON to convert to YAML — a JSON string, or the value itself.

tool_signatures.name: latency_benchmark
tool_signatures.description: Measure response time of one or more HTTP endpoints (GET/POST). Runs N iterations and returns min/max/avg/p95 latency. Useful for API and MCP server benchmarking.

endpoints.description: Endpoints to benchmark. Accepts a single URL string, an array of URL strings, or an array of {url, method?, body?, headers?, label?} objects.

iterations.description: Number of iterations per endpoint (default: 3, max: 10)

tool_signatures.name: levenshtein_distance
tool_signatures.description: Compute the Levenshtein (edit) distance and normalized similarity ratio between two strings. Supports batch comparison. Useful for fuzzy string matching, deduplication, and test result comparison.

tool_signatures.name: lint_commit_message
tool_signatures.description: Validate a git commit message against the Conventional Commits spec (feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, test, chore, ci, perf, build). Returns compliance score, breaking change detection, and actionable suggestions.

strict.description: Enforce strict rules: max 72-char subject, imperative mood check (default: false)

tool_signatures.name: list_llm_models
tool_signatures.description: List all LLM models available on ia-qa.com with their provider, API endpoint, and capabilities. Filter by provider name (e.g. "Groq", "HuggingFace", "OpenAI") or return the full catalog. Use this to discover which models are available before calling an LLM API, or to compare providers.

provider.description: Filter by provider name (case-insensitive). E.g. "Groq", "HuggingFace", "OpenAI", "Anthropic", "Google", "DeepSeek", "xAI", "Ollama". Omit for full catalog.

tool_signatures.name: list_local_tests
tool_signatures.description: Discover .ia-eval.yaml LLM test suite files in the project directory. Scans CWD and standard sub-directories (evals/, tests/, contracts/). Returns file paths ready to pass to run_eval_contract.

dir.description: Directory to scan (defaults to server CWD)

tool_signatures.name: llm_fit_finder
tool_signatures.description: Find the best LLM for a given use case. Compares 30+ cloud API models and 12+ local models by cost, speed, benchmarks, features and VRAM requirements. Returns ranked recommendations with cost simulation. No API key needed.

mode.description: cloud (API models) or local (Ollama/self-hosted). Default: cloud

vram_gb.description: GPU VRAM in GB (only for mode=local). Default: 16

features.description: Required features: vision, function_calling, json_mode, streaming, reasoning

use_case.description: Primary use case: chatbot | code | rag | summarization | classification | reasoning | agents | multilingual

max_budget.description: Maximum monthly budget in USD (based on tokens_per_day)

quantization.description: Quantization (only for mode=local): Q4_K_M | Q8_0 | FP16. Default: Q4_K_M

tool_signatures.name: llm_format_check
tool_signatures.description: Validate that an LLM output matches an expected format: JSON, Markdown, code block, bullet list, numbered list, table, YAML, XML, or custom regex. Essential for structured output testing.

regex_pattern.description: Custom regex pattern (only when expected_format is "regex")

tool_signatures.name: llm_generate
tool_signatures.description: Generate text using open-source LLM models hosted on Groq (ultra-fast) or HuggingFace Inference (serverless). No API key required — the server provides its own keys. Supported models: Qwen3 32B, Gemma 4 27B, Gemma 3 27B, Llama 3.3 70B, Llama 4 Scout, DeepSeek R1, Mistral Small 24B, and more. Use list_llm_models to see the full catalog. Rate-limited to prevent abuse.

model.description: Model ID (default: "qwen/qwen3-32b"). Server-keyed whitelist only — Groq: qwen/qwen3-32b, llama-3.3-70b-versatile, meta-llama/llama-4-scout-17b-16e-instruct, llama-3.1-8b-instant; HuggingFace: Qwen/Qwen3-32B, meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, google/gemma-3-27b-it, and more. Other ids from list_llm_models are BYOK-only and will be rejected.

prompt.description: The user prompt / instruction to send to the model

system.description: Optional system prompt to set context or persona

tool_signatures.name: llm_json_schema_check
tool_signatures.description: Validate that an LLM JSON output matches a JSON Schema definition. Tests required fields, types, enums, nested objects, and arrays. Critical for function-calling and structured output testing.

output.description: The LLM JSON output (raw string, will be parsed)

schema.description: JSON Schema (draft-07 subset) to validate against

tool_signatures.name: llm_output_validator
tool_signatures.description: Validate an LLM response against QA criteria: format checks (JSON, code, markdown), content rules (must-include, must-not-include), length constraints, language detection, and safety patterns. Essential for QA testing LLM-powered features.

output.description: The LLM output text to validate

max_length.description: Maximum character length for the output

min_length.description: Minimum character length for the output

check_safety.description: Check for PII patterns (emails, phones, SSN), profanity signals, and prompt leakage

must_include.description: Comma-separated strings that MUST appear in the output

must_not_include.description: Comma-separated strings that must NOT appear (e.g. "TODO, FIXME, undefined, NaN")

check_json_schema.description: If expected_format is JSON, provide required keys as comma-separated list to validate the structure

expected_language.description: Expected language of the output (en, fr, es, de…). Checks for common words.

tool_signatures.name: lorem_ipsum
tool_signatures.description: Generate Lorem Ipsum placeholder text for UI mockups, design prototypes, or test data population. Configurable paragraphs (1–10), sentences per paragraph (1–20), and approximate words per sentence (3–30).

paragraphs.description: Number of paragraphs to generate (1–10, default: 1)

tool_signatures.name: mcp_schema_lint
tool_signatures.description: Lint an MCP tool definition for best practices: naming conventions, description quality, schema completeness, required fields consistency, description length. Returns actionable warnings.

tool_definition.description: MCP tool definition object with name, description, inputSchema

tool_signatures.name: mcp_server_evaluate
tool_signatures.description: Run a full compliance evaluation against a live MCP server URL. Tests: server reachability (ping), manifest discovery (GET /mcp), schema quality (snake_case names, descriptions, inputSchema), JSON-RPC 2.0 test call, and P50/P95 latency. Returns a PASS/FIX/BLOCK verdict with a 0-100 score and per-check details.

url.description: Base URL of the MCP server (e.g. https://ia-qa.com or http://localhost:3001)

test_tool_name.description: Specific tool name to use in the JSON-RPC test call (defaults to the first tool in the manifest)

tool_signatures.name: mcp_server_health_check
tool_signatures.description: Generate a health check report for an MCP server's tool manifest. Validates tool definitions, schema quality, naming conventions, and documentation completeness. Paste the server manifest JSON to audit.

strict.description: Enable strict mode: also check for optional best practices (examples, default values, descriptions > 20 chars)

manifest.description: MCP server manifest JSON (the response from GET /mcp or tools/list)

tool_signatures.name: merge_json
tool_signatures.description: Deep merge two JSON objects. Supports three array strategies: replace (default), concat, or unique (dedup concat). Nested objects are recursively merged — override takes precedence for primitives.

base.description: The base JSON object (merged into) — a JSON string, or the object itself.

override.description: The override JSON object (takes precedence) — a JSON string, or the object itself.

array_strategy.description: Array merge strategy: replace (default), concat, or unique

tool_signatures.name: metamorphic_check
tool_signatures.description: Reference-free stability primitive: instead of comparing an answer to a ground truth, it checks that an assistant's answer stays INVARIANT when the QUESTION is transformed (typo, casing, paraphrase, reordering, translation). Catches the failure class no reference answer can expose — an assistant that handles one phrasing well and a trivial variant of it badly. You bring the outputs (no model is called), so it is deterministic and free in tfidf mode. Relations: case (θ .95), typo (.90), paraphrase (.80), reorder (.80), translation (.75, embeddings only), specialization (.60, ADVISORY — directional, never gated). Returns PASS / FAIL / INVALID, where INVALID means the BASE answer was a refusal or too short so invariance was never measurable — an assistant that refuses every variant would otherwise score a perfect 1.0. Use run_semantic_tests alongside it: invariance without a correctness floor is a green light for a broken assistant.

output.description: Required — the answer your system produced for the original question.

question.description: Optional — the original question, echoed back in the output for readability.

base.description: The reference run: the original question and the answer your system produced for it.

mode.description: tfidf (default): free, lexical, deterministic — but a genuine paraphrase rarely reaches 0.80, so gate on case/typo and treat paraphrase as a trend. embeddings: OpenAI text-embedding-3-small, true semantic similarity, requires api_key. translation requires this mode.

api_key.description: OpenAI API key — required only when mode is embeddings.

output.description: Required — the answer your system produced for the transformed question.

question.description: Optional — the transformed question, echoed back for readability.

relation.description: Transformation applied to the QUESTION. Decides the metric and the default threshold.

variants.description: Answers produced for transformed versions of the same question, each tagged with the relation that was applied.

thresholds.description: Per-relation threshold overrides. Calibrate on your own corpus before gating — the defaults are starting points, not measurements.

require_all.description: If true (default), every gated variant must pass. If false, one passing gated variant is enough.

min_length.description: Minimum base answer length in chars (default 40).

must_not_match.description: Refusal patterns, matched case-insensitively in the FIRST 200 CHARS of the base answer (refusals lead; matching anywhere would flag a long correct answer that merely mentions one). Replaces the FR+EN default list, never merges — pass [] to disable.

baseline_guard.description: Correctness floor applied to the BASE answer before anything is scored. Failing it returns INVALID, not FAIL.

tool_signatures.name: minify_js
tool_signatures.description: Minify a JavaScript snippet, function, class, or module up to 50 KB using Terser. Returns minified code and byte savings. Use when embedding scripts in HTML templates, report payloads, or injecting inline code programmatically.

tool_signatures.name: mock_from_schema
tool_signatures.description: Generate realistic mock data from a JSON Schema. Supports all common types (string, number, integer, boolean, array, object, null), format hints (email, date, date-time, uri, uuid), enum, const, and nested schemas. Perfect for testing MCP tools with realistic data.

seed.description: Optional seed string for deterministic output (uses first char codes)

count.description: Number of mock objects to generate (default: 1, max: 20)

schema.description: The JSON Schema to generate from — a JSON string, or the schema object itself.

tool_signatures.name: model_info
tool_signatures.description: Get detailed specs for an AI model: context window, pricing per 1K tokens, knowledge cutoff, provider, multimodal support, reasoning capabilities, and feature list. Covers 30+ models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, DeepSeek, Meta, Mistral, Cohere, xAI.

tool_signatures.name: multimodal_eval_guide
tool_signatures.description: Unified tool for multimodal AI evaluation: set action=guide for reference thresholds/interpretation (CLIP, FID, VQA), or set action=clip_score / fid_score / vqa_accuracy / pipeline to compute real metrics via HuggingFace Inference API and VLM BYOK calls. One tool for both reference and computation.

vqa.description: [pipeline] VQA config object (same inputs as vqa_accuracy).

text.description: [clip_score only] Text description to compare against the image.

score.description: [guide only] Optional score value to interpret.

action.description: guide (default) = reference thresholds/interpretation. clip_score/fid_score/vqa_accuracy = compute that metric. pipeline = run all three.

api_key.description: [vqa_accuracy] Your API key for the provider (BYOK).

tool_signatures.name: needle_haystack_generate
tool_signatures.description: Generate a "needle in a haystack" test: embeds a target fact into a large block of filler text at a specified position. Use this to test LLM context window retrieval accuracy. Returns the full haystack, the question to ask, and metadata. No API key needed.

needle.description: The fact to hide (e.g. "The secret code is ALPHA-42")

tokens.description: Target haystack size in tokens (default: 5000, max: 100000)

question.description: The question to ask the LLM (e.g. "What is the secret code?")

tool_signatures.name: normalize_vector
tool_signatures.description: L2-normalize a float vector (produce a unit vector with norm=1). Required by many vector DBs (Pinecone, Qdrant cosine). Supports batch normalization of up to 1000 vectors.

batch.description: Batch of vectors to normalize (overrides vector)

tool_signatures.name: normalize_whitespace
tool_signatures.description: Normalize whitespace: trim trailing spaces, collapse blank lines, normalize line endings (LF/CRLF), convert tabs to spaces. Useful for cleaning code, configs, and text before processing.

trim_lines.description: Trim trailing whitespace from each line (default: true)

tab_to_spaces.description: Convert tabs to N spaces (omit to keep tabs)

collapse_blanks.description: Collapse 3+ consecutive blank lines to 2 (default: true)

tool_signatures.name: number_base_convert
tool_signatures.description: Convert numbers between bases: decimal, binary, octal, hexadecimal, or any base 2–36. Auto-detects 0x, 0b, 0o prefixes.

to_base.description: Target base 2–36 (omit to get all common bases)

tool_signatures.name: openapi_validate
tool_signatures.description: Validate the structure of an OpenAPI 3.x specification (JSON or YAML). Checks required top-level fields (openapi, info.title, info.version, paths), validates each operation (responses, operationId uniqueness), detects undeclared $ref components, and flags missing 2xx responses. Returns a PASS/FAIL verdict, a 0–100 compliance score, and a list of errors and warnings with JSON-pointer locations. Use before publishing an API spec or generating SDK code.

input.description: The OpenAPI 3.x spec — a JSON string, a YAML string, or the already-parsed spec object.

tool_signatures.name: optimize_prompt_tokens
tool_signatures.description: Compress an LLM prompt by removing filler words, verbose phrases, duplicate sentences, and unnecessary whitespace. Returns optimized text with token savings breakdown. 100% deterministic, no API key needed.

options.description: Toggle optimization steps (all true by default)

tool_signatures.name: parse_csv
tool_signatures.description: Parse a CSV string into a JSON array of objects (or raw arrays). Handles RFC 4180 quoted fields, escaped quotes, and custom delimiters. Use when processing spreadsheet exports, data imports, or structured text pipelines where the source is CSV. Supports up to 200 KB.

header.description: Treat the first row as headers (default: true)

tool_signatures.name: parse_http_headers
tool_signatures.description: Parse a raw HTTP headers block into a structured JSON object. Detects multi-value headers, masks Authorization values, and optionally audits for missing security headers (HSTS, CSP, X-Frame-Options, etc.).

headers.description: Raw HTTP headers (one "Name: Value" per line)

analyze_security.description: Audit for missing security headers (default: true)

tool_signatures.name: post_jira_comment
tool_signatures.description: Post the output of jira_to_test_suite as a formatted comment on the source Jira ticket. Converts Gherkin, E2E steps, API tests, and ambiguities into Atlassian Document Format (ADF). STATEFUL — creates a comment on the issue.

test_suite.description: The test_suite object from jira_to_test_suite result

tool_signatures.name: pr_gatekeeper
tool_signatures.description: Compound quality gate for pull requests. Runs three sequential checks: (1) secret detection — scans diff for API keys, tokens, passwords matching 16 regex patterns; (2) bug analysis — heuristic scan for eval(), innerHTML, empty catch, console.log, TODO/FIXME; (3) commit message linting against Conventional Commits spec. Returns gate verdict (PASS/WARN/BLOCK), blockers, and actionable warnings. Use before merging any code change.

diff.description: Unified git diff (output of `git diff HEAD`)

context.description: Optional: PR title or description for richer bug analysis

commit_message.description: The commit message to lint (e.g. "feat(auth): add OAuth2 login")

tool_signatures.name: prompt_injection_scan
tool_signatures.description: Scan user input or prompts for common prompt injection patterns. Detects system prompt overrides, jailbreak attempts, role manipulation, encoding tricks, delimiter attacks, template/interpolation injection ({{...}}, ${...}), and context-exfiltration attempts ("repeat everything above").

input.description: The user input or prompt to scan for injection patterns

tool_signatures.name: prompt_template_fill
tool_signatures.description: Fill a prompt template with variables. Supports {{variable}} syntax and {{#if key}}...{{/if}} conditional blocks. Returns the filled prompt and lists unfilled variables.

strict.description: Throw error if any variable is not provided (default: false)

tool_signatures.name: prompt_test_suite
tool_signatures.description: Define a test suite for a prompt: provide the system prompt, user prompt, and expected output criteria. Returns a test plan with scored rubric — use this as input for manual or automated LLM evaluation.

max_tokens.description: Max token budget for the test

check_safety.description: Include safety/PII checks in the rubric

expected_behavior.description: Description of what the LLM should do (free text)

adversarial_prompts.description: Auto-generate adversarial test variants (jailbreak, injection, edge cases)

tool_signatures.name: rag_relevance_rank
tool_signatures.description: Rank an array of text chunks by relevance to a query using TF-IDF scoring. Simulates retrieval ranking for RAG testing without needing embeddings or an API.

chunks.description: Array of text chunks to rank

tool_signatures.name: rate_tool
tool_signatures.description: Give honest usage feedback on an IA-QA MCP tool. Provide a score (1-5) and a comment. Rate low (1-2) if the tool was wrong, irrelevant, or a poor fit; rate high (4-5) only if it genuinely solved your need. Ratings are aggregated on a public dashboard at /devtools/mcp-ratings. Skip rating routine successes — we want signal, not praise. Example: rate_tool({ tool_name: "format_json", score: 2, comment: "Tried to pretty-print a JSON5 file, it rejected trailing commas — not usable for my case." })

comment.description: Strongly encouraged — explain what you were trying to do and whether the tool got you there. Be specific about what was missing, wrong, or a poor fit. This is the most valuable part of the rating. Up to 2000 chars are stored; go over and the response says so (truncated: true) — send the remainder as a second call rather than assuming it landed.

tool_name.description: Name of the MCP tool to rate (e.g. "format_json", "shield_analyze")

tool_signatures.name: redact_pii
tool_signatures.description: Automatically detect and redact Personally Identifiable Information (PII) from text. Replaces emails, phone numbers, SSNs, credit cards, IP addresses, and JWT tokens with [REDACTED_TYPE] placeholders. Safe to use before logging or sending to an LLM.

types.description: Comma-separated types to redact (default: all). Options: email, phone, ssn, credit_card, ip_address, jwt

tool_signatures.name: regex_test
tool_signatures.description: Test a regular expression pattern against an input string and return all matches with their index positions and named capture groups. Use for validating user inputs, extracting structured data from text, or debugging regex patterns. Supports flags g, i, m, s, u, y.

flags.description: Regex flags: g (global), i (case-insensitive), m (multiline), s (dotAll) — default: ""

input.description: The string to test against (max 50 KB)

tool_signatures.name: rerank_evaluate
tool_signatures.description: Evaluate RAG retrieval quality using the NVIDIA neural reranker (nv-rerankqa-mistral-4b-v3). Ranks passages by semantic relevance to a query and computes Precision@k and Recall@k. Optionally accepts ground-truth relevance labels to produce a PASS/FAIL CI/CD verdict.

query.description: The search query or question to rank against

relevant.description: Ground truth: is this passage relevant?

passages.description: Array of passage objects to rank (min 2, max 20)

tool_signatures.name: response_quality_score
tool_signatures.description: Score an LLM response on multiple quality dimensions: relevance, completeness, clarity, conciseness, formatting. Returns a weighted 0-100 score with detailed breakdown.

max_length.description: Ideal max character length (penalize if exceeded)

expected_keywords.description: Keywords that should appear in a good answer

tool_signatures.name: run_eval_contract
tool_signatures.description: Parse a .ia-eval.yaml LLM test suite, call the specified LLM model for each scenario, run all configured scorers, and return a structured JSON report with per-scenario Pass/Fail verdicts and a Markdown summary. Use list_local_tests to discover available test files.

api_keys.description: API keys to use for LLM generation (all optional — falls back to server env vars)

contract_path.description: Absolute or relative path to a .ia-eval.yaml file (required unless inline_contract is provided)

inline_contract.description: Raw contract object (alternative to contract_path). Must contain top-level "metadata" ({name, version, model?, provider?}), "expectations" ({min_score?}), and "scenarios" ([{id, input, ground_truth?}]) — scenarios alone are rejected. Use generate_eval_yaml to scaffold one.

tool_signatures.name: run_pr_gate_pipeline
tool_signatures.description: Review triage for a pull request. Takes a unified git diff (`git diff HEAD`) and returns: diff-lint findings with the lines that produced them, regression impact areas, a risk score 0–100 with the factors that built it (churn, files touched, sensitive paths, whether any test file changed, lint severities), generated test cases, and a PASS / CONDITIONAL / BLOCK recommendation. Advisory: the score measures properties of the diff, not the correctness of the change — it does not read the code semantically and does not replace a reviewer or a static analyser. See notAnalysed in the response.

context.description: Optional PR title or description for richer analysis

git_diff.description: Unified git diff (output of `git diff HEAD` or copied from GitHub diff view)

tool_signatures.name: run_semantic_tests
tool_signatures.description: Semantic assertion primitive: compare actual vs expected text pairs using cosine similarity + ROUGE-L. Two modes: tfidf (default, free, no API key) or embeddings (OpenAI text-embedding-3-small, BYOK, true semantic similarity). Returns per-case PASS/FAIL verdicts and an overall verdict. CI-ready: pipe the JSON verdict field to gate a build.

mode.description: tfidf (default): fast, free, lexical. embeddings: OpenAI text-embedding-3-small, true semantic similarity, requires api_key.

actual.description: The text produced by your LLM/system.

cases.description: Array of (actual, expected) pairs to evaluate.

api_key.description: OpenAI API key — required only when mode is embeddings.

require_all.description: If true (default), all cases must pass for overall PASS. If false, at least one case passing returns PASS.

tool_signatures.name: run_vlm_test_suite
tool_signatures.description: Run a test suite against a Vision-Language Model (VLM) — send an image (URL or base64) + N test cases (each with a question + assertion) to GPT-4o, Claude 3.5, or Gemini. Returns per-case PASS/FAIL verdicts, a pass rate, an overall PASS/WARNING/FAIL verdict (customizable threshold), and latency stats. Assertion types: contains, not_contains, json_format, min_length, max_length, semantic_contains (TF-IDF cosine similarity ≥ 0.4). BYOK: requires your own API key for the target provider.

api_key.description: API key for the model provider (OpenAI sk-, Anthropic sk-ant-, or Google AIzaSy...).

image_url.description: Public URL of the image to evaluate (required unless image_base64 is provided).

threshold.description: Pass rate threshold for overall verdict (default: 80, 0–100).

question.description: Question to ask the VLM about the image.

assertion_type.description: Assertion to run on the VLM response. semantic_contains uses TF-IDF cosine similarity ≥ 0.4.

assertion_value.description: Expected value for the assertion (not needed for json_format).

test_cases.description: Array of test cases to run.

image_base64.description: Base64-encoded image data (required unless image_url is provided).

system_prompt.description: Optional system prompt sent to the VLM.

image_mime_type.description: MIME type of the image if using image_base64 (default: image/jpeg).

tool_signatures.name: run_vlm_test_suite_batch
tool_signatures.description: Compare multiple VLMs on the same test suite in parallel — send an image (URL or base64) + N test cases to all models simultaneously. Returns per-model PASS/FAIL verdicts, pass rates, latency stats, and a comparison table. Assertion types: contains, not_contains, json_format, min_length, max_length, semantic_contains. BYOK: requires API keys for each provider.

models.description: Array of model IDs to compare (runs in parallel).

api_keys.description: Map of model ID → API key. Example: { "gpt-4o": "sk-...", "claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022": "sk-ant-..." }

image_url.description: Public URL of the image to evaluate (required unless image_base64 is provided).

threshold.description: Pass rate threshold for overall verdict (default: 80, 0–100).

question.description: Question to ask the VLM about the image.

assertion_type.description: Assertion to run on the VLM response.

assertion_value.description: Expected value for the assertion (not needed for json_format).

test_cases.description: Array of test cases to run against every model.

image_base64.description: Base64-encoded image data (required unless image_url is provided).

system_prompt.description: Optional system prompt sent to every VLM.

image_mime_type.description: MIME type of the image if using image_base64 (default: image/jpeg).

tool_signatures.name: score_geo_signals
tool_signatures.description: Analyze a webpage <head> HTML (or full HTML) for GEO (Generative Engine Optimization) signals. Returns a score /60 with per-check results and improvement tips. GEO = optimizing pages for AI-powered search engines (ChatGPT Search, Perplexity, etc.).

head_html.description: Raw HTML of the <head> section (or full page HTML) to analyze

tool_signatures.name: search_jira_issues
tool_signatures.description: Search Jira using JQL (Jira Query Language). Returns matching issues with key fields. Ideal for finding open bugs, sprint tickets, or issues by label/assignee/component. BYOK — credentials transit in-memory only, never stored.

jql.description: JQL query string, e.g. "project = PROJ AND status = Open AND assignee = currentUser() ORDER BY priority DESC"

fields.description: Fields per issue. Default: summary, status, assignee, priority, issuetype, labels, created, updated

tool_signatures.name: secret_scan
tool_signatures.description: Scan text or code for leaked secrets: API keys (AWS, GCP, Azure, OpenAI, Anthropic, Stripe, GitHub, GitLab, Slack, Twilio, SendGrid, HuggingFace), private keys (RSA/EC/PGP), JWTs, database connection strings, Bearer tokens, and Basic auth headers. Returns a list of findings with type, severity, line number, and a redacted preview. Use before committing code, sharing logs, or sending text to an LLM. 100% regex-based, zero network calls.

input.description: Text or code to scan for secrets

types.description: Comma-separated types to scan (default: all). Options: aws, gcp, azure, openai, anthropic, stripe, github, gitlab, slack, twilio, sendgrid, huggingface, jwt, private_key, connection_string, bearer, basic_auth

tool_signatures.name: security_headers_check
tool_signatures.description: Analyse the HTTP security headers of a public URL OR of raw response headers you paste in. Grades each header (A–F) for: Strict-Transport-Security, Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, X-XSS-Protection, Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy, Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy, and Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy. Returns an overall score (0–100), per-header grades, missing headers, and fix snippets for Express, Nginx, and Apache. For localhost/private targets the remote server cannot reach, pass the `headers` parameter instead of `url`.

url.description: Optional. Full public URL to check (e.g. https://example.com). Omit it entirely when using `headers`. The server cannot reach localhost/private IPs.

headers.description: Optional, and sufficient on its own (no url needed). The response headers to grade, either as an object {"strict-transport-security": "max-age=...", ...} or as the raw header block pasted as a string (e.g. `curl -sI` output). Use this to audit a local server the remote MCP cannot reach.

tool_signatures.name: shield_analyze
tool_signatures.description: Run a comprehensive AI guardrail analysis on an LLM response. Orchestrates 6 deterministic safety checks plus an optional LLM-powered deep analysis in parallel: hallucination detection (grounding score), prompt injection scan, toxicity scan, output validation (PII/safety), guardrail rules, response quality scoring, and AI verdict (via Qwen, Gemma, Llama, etc.). Returns a unified PASS/FIX/BLOCK verdict with a 0-100 safety score, per-check results, and actionable fix recommendations. Use this as a single-call safety gate before surfacing any LLM output to users.

model.description: LLM model for AI-powered deep analysis (default: "qwen/qwen3-32b"). Set to "none" to skip LLM check. Supports any model from list_llm_models.

rules.description: Optional guardrail rules array (same format as guardrail_test tool)

prompt.description: Optional original prompt (used for quality scoring and injection detection)

source.description: Optional reference/source text for hallucination grounding check

tool_signatures.name: similarity_score
tool_signatures.description: Compute text similarity between reference and hypothesis using multiple metrics: Cosine (BoW, TF-IDF), Jaccard, ROUGE-1, ROUGE-2, ROUGE-L, and BLEU. No API key needed. Ideal for LLM eval (expected vs actual), RAG quality checks, and NLG benchmarking. Supports batch mode.

batch.description: Batch mode: array of {reference, hypothesis} pairs.

threshold.description: Optional pass/fail threshold (0-1). Applies to ROUGE-L F1 score.

tool_signatures.name: sort_lines
tool_signatures.description: Sort, deduplicate, reverse, or filter lines of text. Useful for cleaning import lists, dependencies, log files, and config entries.

trim.description: Trim whitespace from each line (default: true)

filter.description: For "filter": keep lines containing this substring (case-insensitive)

tool_signatures.name: split_chunks
tool_signatures.description: Split text into chunks of at most N tokens (cl100k_base: ~4 chars/token) with optional overlap. Designed for RAG ingestion pipelines.

tool_signatures.name: ssl_certificate_check
tool_signatures.description: Analyse the SSL/TLS certificate of any HTTPS host. Returns certificate subject, issuer, validity dates, days until expiry, protocol version, cipher suite, key exchange info, and an overall grade (A+, A, B, C, F). Detects expired, self-signed, and weak certificates. Use this to audit TLS posture before production deployment or during security reviews.

host.description: Hostname to check (e.g. example.com). Do not include https:// prefix.

tool_signatures.name: strip_markdown
tool_signatures.description: Strip all Markdown formatting (headers, bold, italic, code fences, links, lists) from text and return clean plain text. Run this before injecting scraped documentation, README files, or user content into an LLM prompt to eliminate redundant markup tokens and reduce cost.

input.description: Markdown text to convert to plain text

tool_signatures.name: system_prompt_builder
tool_signatures.description: Build a structured system prompt from components: role, task, constraints, output format, tone, language, and examples. Generates a production-ready system prompt with token estimate.

tool_signatures.name: test_skill
tool_signatures.description: Validate a SKILL.md definition (Cursor / GitHub Copilot / Windsurf) by auto-generating trigger-positive and trigger-negative scenarios, running each through the model with the skill injected as a system prompt, and scoring trigger accuracy + step adherence. Returns a PASS/FIX/BLOCK verdict with per-scenario breakdown. Uses Groq llama-3.3-70b by default (server key, no api_key needed). Pass api_key + model to use your own provider.

model.description: LLM model ID to use for both scenario generation and testing (e.g. gpt-4o-mini, claude-3-5-haiku-20241022). Defaults to llama-3.3-70b-versatile (Groq, server key).

api_key.description: API key for the chosen model provider. Not required when using the default Groq model.

skill_md.description: Full content of the SKILL.md file to test. Must include a name, a "Use when:" trigger description, and at least one step.

scenario_count.description: Number of test scenarios to generate: half trigger-positive, half trigger-negative. Default: 6.

tool_signatures.name: text_stats
tool_signatures.description: Compute comprehensive statistics for any text: character count (with and without spaces), word count, line count, sentence count, paragraph count, and estimated reading time in minutes. Use for validating form field lengths, evaluating LLM output verbosity, or content auditing.

tool_signatures.name: timestamp_convert
tool_signatures.description: Convert between Unix timestamps (seconds or milliseconds) and ISO-8601 / UTC date strings. Auto-detects epoch vs. millisecond format. Omit input to get the current time. Returns iso, unix_s, unix_ms, utc, date, and time fields.

input.description: Unix timestamp (number, seconds or ms) or ISO date string. Omit to get the current time.

tool_signatures.name: token_budget_calculator
tool_signatures.description: Plan token allocation across system prompt, user input, context/RAG chunks, and expected output. Warns if budget exceeds model context window. Supports 25+ models.

user_input.description: Actual user input text (will estimate tokens)

system_prompt.description: Actual system prompt text (will estimate tokens)

context_tokens.description: Token count for RAG context / documents

tool_signatures.name: toxicity_scan
tool_signatures.description: Scan text for toxic language, bias indicators, profanity, and harmful content categories. Returns risk scores per category. Useful for LLM safety guardrail testing.

tool_signatures.name: transform_json_array
tool_signatures.description: Transform a JSON array using common operations: pluck (extract specific fields), filter (by field value), sort_by (field), group_by (field), count_by (field), uniq_by (field). Useful for processing MCP tool results and LLM structured outputs.

n.description: For first_n / last_n: number of items

path.description: Optional dot-notation path to the array within the JSON object (e.g. "data.items")

field.description: Field to operate on (for sort_by, group_by, count_by, uniq_by, filter)

input.description: The JSON containing an array (or an object with an array at `path`) — a JSON string, or the value itself.

tool_signatures.name: truncate_to_tokens
tool_signatures.description: Truncate text to at most N tokens (cl100k_base: ~4 chars/token) to avoid exceeding an LLM context window. Optionally keeps the end of the text instead of the start (useful for keeping recent conversation history). Reports whether truncation occurred and the estimated token count.

from_end.description: Keep the end of the text instead of the start (default: false)

max_tokens.description: Maximum number of tokens to keep

tool_signatures.name: unescape_html
tool_signatures.description: Convert HTML entities (&, <, >, ", ', and numeric &#NNN;) back to plain characters. Use when processing HTML-encoded text from APIs, email content, or legacy database fields before passing to an LLM or displaying to users.

tool_signatures.name: url_decode
tool_signatures.description: Decode a percent-encoded URL string back to plain text. Use when parsing query parameters from raw URLs or when displaying encoded values to users.

tool_signatures.name: url_encode
tool_signatures.description: Percent-encode a string for safe use in URLs. Call this before programmatically building query strings, path segments, or form-encoded bodies to prevent injection and malformed URLs.

tool_signatures.name: validate_agent_trajectory
tool_signatures.description: Run declarative assertions on an agent trace (OpenAI tool-call messages, LangChain run trees, or plain text logs). No LLM call — deterministic. Assertion types: order (tool A before B), must_call, must_not_call, max_calls, min_calls, no_error, recovery (agent continues after error). Returns per-assertion PASS/FAIL, parsed steps, and an overall verdict. Use this to gate CI/CD on agent behavior correctness.

trace.description: Agent execution trace as JSON (OpenAI messages array, LangChain run tree) or plain text log (Thought/Action/Observation format).

tool.description: Tool name to check (for must_call, must_not_call, max_calls, min_calls).

after.description: [order] Tool that must be called after.

before.description: [order] Tool that must be called first.

assertions.description: List of assertions to validate against the trace.

tool_signatures.name: validate_email
tool_signatures.description: Validate an email address against RFC 5322 syntax before storing it, sending a transactional email, or adding it to a mailing list. Returns { valid, email } — use this to avoid bounces and malformed data.

tool_signatures.name: validate_mcp_response
tool_signatures.description: Validate that an MCP tool response conforms to expected format, schema, and content rules. Use this to QA-test any MCP server tool. Supply the tool's actual JSON result and a set of checks to perform.

response.description: The MCP tool result as a JSON string to validate

min_items.description: If response is an array, minimum number of items expected

required_keys.description: Comma-separated list of keys that MUST exist in the response (dot-notation for nested: "data.id, data.name")

actual_latency.description: Actual measured latency in ms (from the call)

forbidden_keys.description: Comma-separated list of keys that MUST NOT exist (e.g. "password, secret, token")

max_size_bytes.description: Maximum acceptable response size in bytes

max_response_ms.description: Maximum acceptable latency in ms (will be compared if provided)

tool_signatures.name: validate_url
tool_signatures.description: Parse and validate a URL. Returns decomposed components: protocol, hostname, port, path, query parameters, hash, and origin.

tool_signatures.name: vector_quantize
tool_signatures.description: Simulate int8 or int4 quantization of float32 embedding vectors. Reduces storage by 4x (int8) or 8x (int4). Returns quantized values, scale factor, and precision loss (MSE). Useful for understanding vector DB compression trade-offs.

tool_signatures.name: vector_similarity
tool_signatures.description: Compute similarity/distance between two float vectors: cosine similarity, dot product, Euclidean and Manhattan distance. Essential for vector DB relevance scoring, embedding evaluation, and nearest-neighbor testing.

vector_a.description: First vector as array of floats

vector_b.description: Second vector as array of floats

tool_signatures.name: vector_stats
tool_signatures.description: Compute statistics for a float vector or matrix of vectors: mean, std, L2 norm, min, max, sparsity, top-K indices. Useful for debugging embedding quality and analyzing vector distributions in a vector DB.

top_k.description: Return indices of top K absolute values (default: 5)

matrix.description: Matrix of vectors (overrides vector). Returns per-vector + matrix-level stats. Required unless `vector` is given.

vector.description: Single vector to analyze. Required unless `matrix` is given.

tool_signatures.name: web_security_audit
tool_signatures.description: Run a comprehensive web security audit combining headers, SSL, CORS, and cookies checks — then use an LLM to produce a prioritised remediation plan. Orchestrates security_headers_check + ssl_certificate_check + cors_test + cookie_security_audit in parallel, merges all findings, then asks an AI model to: (1) rank vulnerabilities by real-world exploitability, (2) generate a remediation roadmap, (3) produce fix code snippets for the detected stack. Returns both raw audit data and the AI analysis. Use this as a one-click security posture assessment.

model.description: LLM model for AI analysis (default: "qwen/qwen3-32b"). Set to "none" to skip AI analysis.

api_key.description: Your Groq or HuggingFace API key. Required to enable AI analysis.

tool_signatures.name: webhook_endpoint_create
tool_signatures.description: Create a temporary webhook endpoint that captures incoming HTTP requests for one hour. Returns the webhook id, public URL, expiration timestamp, and current request count. Use together with webhook_endpoint_requests to inspect captured payloads.

base_url.description: Optional public base URL. Default: https://ia-qa.com/mcp/webhook

tool_signatures.name: webhook_endpoint_requests
tool_signatures.description: Fetch the requests captured by a webhook created with webhook_endpoint_create. Returns the newest requests first with method, headers, query params, body payload, and timestamps.

limit.description: Maximum number of requests to return (1-100, default: 20)

tool_signatures.name: word_frequency
tool_signatures.description: Analyze word frequency in text. Returns top N words with counts and percentages. Supports English stopword filtering. Useful for content analysis, keyword extraction, and LLM output analysis.

tool_signatures.name: xml_to_json
tool_signatures.description: Convert an XML string to a JSON object. Supports attributes, nested elements, arrays, CDATA, and namespaces. Options: parse numbers, parse booleans, ignore attributes.

tool_signatures.name: yaml_to_json
tool_signatures.description: Parse a YAML string and return the equivalent JSON value. The reverse of json_to_yaml. Supports nested objects, arrays, anchors, aliases, multi-document streams, and all scalar types. Use when processing config files, CI/CD pipeline definitions, or OpenAPI specs authored in YAML.

multi.description: If true, parse all documents in a multi-document stream and return an array (default: false)
